intervals.note: Year precision: the INR laboratory page says the 3200-channel telescope was launched in 1978. A 2002 collaboration paper says it 'was constructed late in 1977' and physics began later; a 2013 paper counts continuous measurements 'since December of 1978'. The interval is open: the latest paper read (PoS(MUTO2022)035, data to 31 December 2021) says the facility 'has been uninterruptedly used' for the neutrino-burst search since mid-1980; no source confirms operation in 2026.

name: Baksan Underground Scintillation Telescope
notes: Primary kind cosmic_ray: the INR page calls it a multipurpose installation for astrophysics, particle physics and cosmic rays. Its best-known results are the neutrino-burst search (it recorded neutrinos from SN 1987A: astro-ph/0212499) and, as secondary kinds, atmospheric-neutrino-induced upward muons.
Not in the SAGE laboratory: the telescope hall is about 550 m inside the horizontal tunnel (INR page) at about 850 m w.e.; the SAGE gallium-germanium laboratory is 3.5 km in at 4700 m w.e.

physics_goals.quote: БПСТ - многоцелевая подземная установка, предназначенная для решения большого круга проблем астрофизики, физики элементарных частиц и космических лучей (к.л.).
physics_goals.value: A multipurpose underground installation for problems of astrophysics, elementary-particle physics and cosmic rays; in practice a continuous search for neutrino bursts from stellar collapse, atmospheric-neutrino-induced muons and indirect dark-matter searches

summary.plain: A four-storey building of 3,184 liquid-scintillator tanks inside Mount Andyrchi in the Caucasus, 850 metres of rock-equivalent deep. Running since 1978, it counts cosmic-ray muons and neutrinos, and has watched for a burst from an exploding star in our Galaxy since 1980.
summary.technical: Multipurpose underground scintillation telescope (17 x 17 x 11 m^3; four horizontal and four vertical planes of 3184 standard 0.7 x 0.7 x 0.3 m^3 liquid-scintillator counters, 330 t) at 850 m w.e. in the Baksan Neutrino Observatory (INR RAS). Neutrino-burst monitor (240 t target): 35.8 yr of live time to 2021, no Galactic collapse candidate, f < 0.064 per year (90 % CL); also upward-muon, indirect WIMP and GW170817 neutrino searches.
